name: notice-board-visit-two-boards-v1
description: ⭐ DEAN'S TWO-BOARD FIX FOR THE NOTICE BOARD VISIT, RULED 11/09/2026, AND THIS IS THE ARM THAT CARRIES IT. It is built as an ARM and not as the default: measure it against its control on identical reference-v15 seeds, put the numbers in front of Dean, and only then flip anything. The design it varies is docs/notice-board-visit-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md, rules S1-S16. THE RULE IN ONE LINE: self-visiting stays BANNED, and AT TWO SEATS each player lays out TWO Notice Boards - their own suit's, plus one more drawn AT RANDOM from the suits nobody is farming - with the fifth board unused. At three and four seats it is one board each and the rest are unused, which is exactly the control, so THIS VARIANT DIFFERS FROM overlays/notice-board-visit-no-self-v1.overlay.json AT TWO SEATS ONLY. Everything else is that arm: the bonus is still to play ONE card from your hand onto a Notice Board, taken FIRST, and the card rests on the board it was played to until that board's OWNER harvests it into their barn, which is their whole payment and there is no other. ⛔ ITS CONTROL IS overlays/notice-board-visit-no-self-v1.overlay.json AND THE THREE-SEAT AND FOUR-SEAT COLUMNS ARE THE SAME RULES, NOT MERELY SIMILAR ONES. rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats sets 1 at three seats and 1 at four, which is the base value, so those two columns MUST REPRODUCE THE CONTROL ON IDENTICAL SEEDS and ANY DIFFERENCE THERE IS A LEAK RATHER THAN A FINDING - a bot term reading the new knob it should not read, a setup draw consuming an rng call it did not consume before, or a report line counting boards instead of seats. Read those two columns against the control FIRST, confirm they are identical, and only then read the two-seat column, which is the only place this arm is a different game. ⭐ WHY IT EXISTS, AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Four corners of a 2x2 were run at 4,820 games each on the morning of 11/09/2026, and the design's own thesis is that A VISIT PAYS THE PERSON VISITED. With self-visits ON and no centre the bonus rate read 71.2% and the hook 0.44, a FAIL. With self-visits ON and the unclaimed centre on, 78.4% and 0.23, a FAIL. With self-visits OFF and the centre on, 64.7% and 0.31, a FAIL. With self-visits OFF and NO centre, 46.1% and 0.54 - THE ONLY CORNER IN THE WHOLE PASS THAT PASSES THE HOOK, and therefore the only version in which the design works at all. ⛔ AND THAT CORNER STARVES AT TWO PLAYERS: the bonus is used on 28.8% of turns against Dean's own 30% floor, and 17.9% of two-player turns begin with cards in hand and NO LEGAL VISIT, because with self-visiting banned and one board each THERE IS EXACTLY ONE BOARD A SEAT MAY VISIT. Adding ownerless central boards (overlays/notice-board-visit-unclaimed-v1.overlay.json) fixed the rate and DESTROYED THE CROSS-TABLE TRAFFIC: at two players only 14.7% of plays reached a person. ⭐ THE STRUCTURAL LESSON IT MEASURED IS THE WHOLE REASON FOR THIS ARM: THERE ARE ONLY EVER FOUR TARGETS, AND EVERY TARGET ADDED THAT IS NOT A PERSON DILUTES THE PERSON. ⭐ SO THIS ARM ADDS TARGETS THAT ARE PEOPLE, WHICH IS THE THING THE CENTRAL-BOARDS VARIANT GOT WRONG. Targets become 2 / 2 / 3 by seat count - at two seats one rival holding two boards, at three seats two rivals holding one each, at four seats three rivals holding one each - and EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A PERSON, so the hook is not diluted by the fix for the starve. A seat still may never visit its own board, either of them. ⭐ AND THE RANDOM BOARD PAYS ITS OWNER, WHICH IS THIS DESIGN'S CORE LOOP ARRIVING ON A CARD WHOSE POWER ITS OWNER CAN NEVER USE: the extra board's power is usable only by rivals, but every fee paid onto it rests there until its owner harvests it into their barn. A POPULAR BOARD IS INCOME. ⛔ EVERY PASSENGER IS PINNED BY NAME AND HERE IS THE LIST, because the 05/09/2026 lesson is that ruling an arm in rules in its whole bundle and the meeple supply cap shipped at 2 that way without anybody arguing for it. EIGHTEEN LEAVES, IN SIX GROUPS. THE DESIGN ITSELF, four: (1) rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower' - the fourth value, and NOT a repointing of 'card', because 'card' is the v31 control and carries three passengers this design does not want (a BLOCKING board threshold of 2, the standalone free Draw 1 in the bonus slot, and the turn-start meeple spend) and one of the three named controls may never move under an arm it is read against; (2) rules.turn.bonusTiming 'start' - S5, bonus FIRST because a turn visibly ends on the main action, pinned so the arm cannot silently stop being itself if the default ever flips; (3) rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold 3 - S8, and it is a MINIMUM; (4) rules.economy.noticeBoardBlocks false - S8's plus sign, so cards may always be added, nothing ever blocks, and no owner can shut a board by declining to harvest. THE BAN THIS ARM IS BUILT ON, one: (5) rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed false - the corner that passes the hook, and the reason the rest of this arm exists, since that corner is the one that starves at two seats. THE NEW LEAVES, three, and they ARE the variant: (6) rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats.2 = 2, (7) rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats.3 = 1 and (8) rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats.4 = 1. Seven and eight are the BASE values and are pinned anyway, because a map whose other keys are left to the default is a map that can change shape under the arm without anybody noticing, and those two keys are exactly the claim that this arm reproduces its control at three and four seats. ⛔ THE CENTRE, TURNED OFF BY NAME, one, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PIN IN THE FILE: (9) rules.economy.unclaimedBoardsToCentre FALSE. This variant is the ALTERNATIVE to the unclaimed-boards centre and never an addition to it: the centre is the thing that measured 14.7% of plays reaching a person at two seats, and leaving this leaf unpinned is precisely how that passenger rides in if the default ever moves. The three commons knobs that ration a central pile (commonsThreshold, commonsHarvestMin, commonsHarvestTake) are deliberately NOT pinned, on the same ground as the control: with no centre on the table they have no subject, and pinning a subjectless leaf would break the leaf-for-leaf diff this arm is read through. THE COMMONS FEE RULES AND THE COINS, TURNED OFF BY NAME, five: (10) rules.turn.commonsTake 'harvest' - the shipped value, and the only one under which a Harvest is a Harvest; (11) rules.economy.commonsColourMatch false - any card pays for any board; (12) rules.economy.commonsWildPair false, which means nothing without the gate above it and is pinned beside it so the pair can never arrive alone; (13) rules.economy.endgameCoinCost null - the fifteen Endgame cards go back to two cards of their own suit (S14); (14) rules.economy.farmsteadCoinPower false - the whole coin economy of 10/09/2026 is superseded and the Farmstead is a token tray with six printed slots and no rules text (S4). THE MEEPLES, STILL NOWHERE, four: (15) rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour 0, (16) rules.turn.meepleAsCard false, (17) rules.turn.slotToll null and (18) rules.turn.meepleCapPerColour null. All four are already the shipped values and are pinned anyway, because no meeples is part of THIS design rather than something it inherits, and a pin is what stops an inheritance turning into a passenger. ⚠️ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED, AND WHY, because an unexplained absence reads as an oversight. rules.economy.noticeBoardPower.* - the five S12 power numbers as amended by rulings C88 and C89 - are the BASE values every arm in this family reads unchanged; pinning them here would make a repricing invisible to this arm and visible to its control. rules.turn.meepleAsCardGoesTo, rules.turn.paymentSlotToll and rules.turn.paymentHostChoice are pinned ONLY BY PROXY: every one of them is read behind rules.turn.meepleAsCard, which this overlay pins false, so none of them has a subject, and adding three leaves that say nothing would break the leaf-for-leaf diff against the control. workers.roster.* is the DOOR roster and an owned board grants a POWER rather than a door, so its numbers describe nothing here; with rules.economy.unclaimedBoardsToCentre false there is no central board either, so the Apiary GROW-or-SOW seam the unclaimed arm had to rule on HAS NO SUBJECT UNDER THIS ARM. And the engine's hand limit of 7 is the SIMULATOR'S BOUND and not a rule of the game (C7): the table plays with none, and every report header must say so. ⛔ THE OPEN RISKS, RECORDED RATHER THAN ANSWERED, AND NEITHER HAS EVER BEEN MEASURED. (1) THE RANDOM BOARD IS AN ASYMMETRY. Each player's extra board is drawn AT RANDOM, its power is usable only by the opponent, and which board you get is LUCK. It is defensible because a popular board pays its owner, so drawing the board the opponent most wants is drawing an income stream rather than a handicap, but that is an argument and not a reading: a table may simply read it as unfair, and at two seats there is one opponent and nowhere for the luck to average out. Read the visits received per player SPREAD at two seats, and read it by which board a seat drew. (2) TWO BOARDS IS TWO HARVESTS. At two seats each player has twice the board income and twice the harvesting to do, and rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold applies to EACH board separately, so a seat's incoming fee traffic splits across two boards and each fills at half the rate. That may move the BARN GLUT and the GAME LENGTH at two seats and nowhere else, which is exactly the shape of finding this arm is most likely to produce and most likely to have mistaken for a leak. Read the a20 stall on owned boards at two seats hardest of all: a board that fills at half the rate sits under its minimum for twice as long. ⭐ AND THREE CONSEQUENCES NOBODY HAD NAMED, FOUND BY READING THE CODE RATHER THAN THE DESIGN, EVERY ONE OF THEM AN ENGINE DECISION RATHER THAN A LEAF. ⛔ (1) A HELPING HAND COMES ALIVE AT TWO SEATS FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND IT MOVES THE HEADLINE NUMBER. S9 is one use per board per turn, enforced as a latch on the board's CARD ID, so under the control at two seats a seat has exactly one legal target and A Helping Hand's second play CAN NEVER BE TAKEN. Under this arm the one rival holds two boards, so it can. The gap between the bonus rate on the TURN measure and on the PLAYS measure therefore opens at two seats in the arm where it was welded shut in the control, and judging Dean's 30-60% band on plays rather than turns has already cost this project one re-run (09/09/2026). Quote the turn measure, and expect the two measures to diverge at two seats only. ⛔ (2) query.noticeBoardOf RETURNS ONE BOARD AND THE VISIT ENUMERATOR READS THE HOST'S SUIT FOR THE POWER. It finds the FIRST tableau building whose slot is 'noticeboard' and throws if there is none, and enumerateNoticeBoardVisits takes the power's colour from player(state, host).suit rather than from the board card it just found. With two boards in a tableau the first silently wins and the second board's power is read as the owner's own suit, which is the one bug this arm can have and it is silent at every seat count but two. Everything downstream inherits it: the S9 latch is keyed on the card id and so stays a correct partition, but harvest targeting, A21's count and the door mix all read through the same seam. ⚠️ (3) THE EXTRA BOARD'S SUIT NEED NOT HAVE A DECK IN PLAY. island.decksInPlayBySeats is 3 at two seats, so of the three suits nobody is farming only ONE has a deck on the table and two have none at all; the extra board may be drawn from any of the three. That is defensible - a board grants a POWER and never a deck, and the commons put all five actions on the table regardless of who farmed them - but it is a choice nobody has made explicitly, and whether the draw should prefer a suit whose deck is in play is an ENGINE ruling. ⭐ WHAT TO READ, IN ORDER, AND THE FIRST ONE IS NOT THE RATE. (1) THE THREE-SEAT AND FOUR-SEAT COLUMNS AGAINST THE CONTROL, which must be identical: a difference there is a leak and everything below it is unreadable until it is fixed. (2) VISITS RECEIVED PER PLAYER and the OWN / RIVAL split at two seats, where own must read ZERO by construction. (3) The bonus rate on the TURN measure at two seats against Dean's 30% to 60%, which is the 28.8% this arm was ruled to rescue, with the PLAYS measure beside it and the two expected to diverge here for the first time. (4) The share of two-player turns that begin with cards in hand and no legal visit, which read 17.9% in the control and is the starve itself. (5) The hook, which read 0.54 in the control and is the only corner that passes it: if this arm moves the hook DOWN, the fix has cost the thing it was protecting. (6) The spread between the busiest and quietest board at two seats, split by whether a board is a seat's own suit or its randomly drawn one, which is open risk 1 arriving as a number. (7) The a20 stall on owned boards at two seats, which is open risk 2. (8) Barn glut, action inflation, game length and deliveries per player at two seats against three and four, since only the two-seat column can have moved. ⚠️ HOW TO RUN IT: --overlay= with --watchlist, never --sweep=, and always --n=1580 (4,820 games, five mirrors, reference-v15 seeds), paired against overlays/notice-board-visit-no-self-v1.overlay.json on identical seeds. A bare --watchlist is a 1,580-game pilot and must not be quoted beside a real run. Stay on reference-v15 and cut reference-v16 only when Dean rules the variant in. UNBUILT IN THE ENGINE AND UNRUN BEFORE THIS PASS: this file is the data layer only. ⛔ PINNED AT dairyGrowsBuilt 'none' ON 12/09/2026, WHEN THE BASE MOVED TO 'paidWild'. Every number published off this arm was measured BEFORE Dean ruled the Dairy board's follow-on Grow in, so the pin is what keeps this file reproducing what it measured. A new arm that wants the ruled rule should say so by name. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved. ⛔ APIARY PINNED 14/09/2026: Dean ruled the Apiary board's retext in as the shipped default (apiaryPower 'deckGrowWild', "Grow a building using the top card of any deck", the deck card paying any activation cost). This overlay predates it, so apiaryPower is pinned here BY NAME at 'sow' (the S12 Sow 2) and it still replays its own game. ⛔ DELIVERY MEEPLE PINNED 14/09/2026: Dean ruled the delivery meeple ON as the shipped default (rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace 1, meepleSpendTiming 'afterAction', meepleSpendPerTurn 1, meepleSpendDistinctColours false) together with two new island rules, the space choice (rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice true: a delivery names either free space) and the closing draw (rules.turn.closingDrawPerCrate 1: filling a tile draws one card per crate). This overlay predates it, so all six leaves are pinned here BY NAME at their pre-ruling values (deliveryMeepleSpace null, meepleSpendTiming 'start', meepleSpendPerTurn null, meepleSpendDistinctColours false, deliverySpaceChoice false, closingDrawPerCrate 0; 'start' and null are the old inert values, not 'none' and 0) and it still replays its own game.
